title: Derivative of the negative Gaussian quantile
statement: Let $\Phi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function, define $Q(\alpha)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R: \alpha\leq\Phi(t)\}$, and set $I(\alpha)=\varphi(Q(\alpha))$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density. For $a\in(0,1)$, the function $p\mapsto -Q(p)$ is differentiable at $a$ with derivative $-1/I(a)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. For every $a\in(0,1)$, the derivative of $p\mapsto-Q(p)$ at $a$ is $-1/I(a)$.
